about: Single photos of each missile, their marks read by measure.py: the body's outline in pairs across it gives the axis and scale, from the cited diameter. Pixels in the full-resolution photo, x right, y down. Files under references/ (fetch.py).

dvids5373461_aim9_wingtip_rear.view: nearly head-on from AHEAD (not from behind): the seeker dome faces the camera, line of sight about 6-10 deg off the axis, from slightly left of and below the nose; the tail recedes up and to the right
dvids5373461_aim9_wingtip_rear.notes: VIEW: A maintainer at an F/A-18 wingtip; the missile on the wingtip LAU-7 points at the camera, so the photo looks along it from the front, not from behind (the round glass dome with seeker optics faces the camera). Fins in X at both ends; names below use the photo's left/right and up/down because near/far and upper/lower in the brief's side-view sense do not apply. MARKS: body_top_1/body_bottom_1 are the top and bottom of the black nose section's silhouette, which is a circle: three points on its lower arc against the snow, (2100, 1194.5), (2178.2, 1178.2), (2037.3, 1162.7), give centre (2117.4, 1082.2), radius 113.6 px (diameter 227 px = the 5 in body at about the canard station; about 45 px per inch there). The bottom is +-1; the top (dark against the grey body behind, 970.5) agrees with that circle within 2 px. dome_top/dome_bottom are the image top and bottom of the glass dome's rim circle (centre about (2100, 1099), radius 67-68 px horizontally and vertically, so the dome diameter is about 0.59 of the body's, about 3 in); they are the rim's highest and lowest image points, not points on the missile's hanger-side outline. The dome rim's centre sits 17 px left and 17 px below the body circle's centre, the offset of the view from the axis. Canard tips: pointed in this view (tip chords seen end-on), +-3 px; the upper-right canard's tip lies in front of the body behind it and is not separable. Wing tips at the far end are seen end-on against a blurred background, +-3 px (upper-right +-4). The tail body's outline is mostly hidden behind the forward body; only its right side shows (x about 2607-2615 at y 700-785), too short an arc to fit. NOT MARKED: nose (the dome apex is not an outline point here; it projects about 6 px lower-left of the rim centre); fin roots (inside the silhouettes); rollerons; lugs (the hanger side faces the launcher at the left); launcher points (its forward fairing faces the camera). DETAIL PASS (2026-11-09): VIEW: as in photos.json; the wings are at the far end, about 28 px/in there (the three visible tips lie 344-355 px from their common centre, 12.4 in). MARKS: none: the housings' and wheels' thickness cannot be read here. Each wing shows as a band along its span: the upper-right wing nearly edge-on, a bright ridge 7 px wide at half-maximum inboard narrowing to 4.7 px near the tip; the lower-right wing a dark band 20.5 px wide narrowing to 16 px toward the tip; the upper-left wing a lit edge plus a dark face band whose far edge merges with the dark background. No band widens near its tip, where the housing (the outer ~3 in of span) sits, but no band is the wing's thickness either: on the upper-right wing only the lit leading edge separates from the background (the shaded faces and the trees behind are both ~35 in luminance), and the lower-right band includes the planform seen 6-10 deg off its plane (a 15 in chord at 8 deg projects ~2 in). From ahead the housing and wheel also sit behind the wing's own leading-edge profile, showing only where thicker than it. So neither a thickness nor a bound is given. NOT MARKED: housing_thickness_* and rolleron_thickness_* (above); the lower-left wing (hidden behind the forward body); the nozzle (faces away); hangers (face the launcher).

dvids6456802_aim9m_wing_detail.view: close-up of the motor's aft end from the side, camera slightly aft of the nozzle plane and very close (strong perspective); the aft face shows
dvids6456802_aim9m_wing_detail.notes: VIEW: Missile on a build stand, tail to the right, a technician torquing the aft end. Hanger side up; the near-upper wing (stencilled WING ASSEMBLY MARK 1 MOD 2) fills the top left, the near-lower wing runs down toward the camera at the bottom left (sunlit tan rolleron housing and toothed wheel, badly out of focus), so the fins are in X about the hanger. The camera is close and just aft of the nozzle plane: the aft face is visible and the outline bulges right to (1933, 1640). Body width at the aft end is 927 px (about 185 px per inch); the bottom outline is 2104.4 at x 1560 and 2108.3 at x 1830, so the near (aft) end is larger. MARKS: Only one body pair is possible: the top outline is hidden by the near-upper wing forward of x 1495 and by a hanger (the gold-coloured block, x about 1490-1820, y 800-1185, probably the aft hanger) from 1495 to 1820, so the top is measurable only between the hanger and the rim (x 1825-1845, y 1181.0 +-1). Bottom against a dark gap, +-1. tail_top and tail_bottom are where the straight outlines end at the rim; the rim is chamfered and does not fit an ellipse cleanly, so these are +-6 px along x (about 0.03 in). wing_upper_near_root_trailing is the rounded lower-aft corner of the upper wing panel (radius about 15 px; fitted corner of its near-vertical aft edge, x 1498 over y 1220-1300, with its root edge y 1323). Above y 1000 the aft edge leans (x 1429.5 at y 300, 1459.5 at 600, 1490.5 at 900: dx/dy about 0.10, the trailing edge proper) and bends to vertical below 1000, so the trailing-edge line itself meets the root line about 35 px further aft (1534, 1323); the panel's root edge sits on a rail whose lower edge is at y 1335. NOT MARKED: wing tips (the upper tip is above the frame - only the bottom of its rolleron housing plate shows at y 0-100, ending at x 1390; the lower tip and rolleron are out of focus, wheel teeth visible along y 2790-2890 from x about 420 to 980, centre not placeable better than +-20 px); lug front edges (the hanger's forward end is behind the wing); other body pairs; joints. DETAIL PASS (2026-11-09): VIEW: Motor aft end on a build stand, tail to the right, camera about level and ~8 deg aft of the beam (the aft face shows as an ellipse 135 px wide by ~920 tall). Only TWO wings are on this round: the near-upper (stencilled WING ASSEMBLY MARK-1 MOD-2, top left) and the FAR-LOWER (bottom centre-left, x 690-1740, y 2125-3455, behind the body). They are one plane: 11 points on the near-upper trailing edge (y 300-800) and 12 on the far-lower's (y 2206-2733) fit one straight line x = 0.09929 y + 1399.76 with rms 0.7 px, max 1.3 px over 2,400 px; the far-lower's edge emerges from behind the body's bottom silhouette (y ~2125), and leans the opposite way to what a near-lower wing would. The blurred tan wing at bottom left (top edge y ~1690, tan housing and wheel at x 300-1000, y 2400-2900) is NOT on this round: a wing mounted near-lower would emerge from the body at y ~1970 and lean the other way; it is a loose wing in the foreground. No far-upper wing is on the round either (nothing above the body right of the near-upper trailing edge). The sharp rolleron, housing, bracket and teeth the brief placed at x 1300-1650, y 2300-2700 are the FAR-LOWER wing's, at x 690-1740, y 2890-3455; the near-upper wing's tip is above the frame (only its housing's inboard edge shows at y 86-100). MARKS (unsuffixed wing_/housing/rolleron/bracket names are the FAR-LOWER wing; its tip edge is the bottom edge, its trailing edge the right edge; we see its face toward the camera at about 45 deg, so spanwise distances are foreshortened ~0.71 and chordwise ones nearly true): wing_trailing_edge_1-7 the painted far-lower trailing edge (max-gradient, +-1 px). wing_tip_edge_1-7 the painted tip edge left of the housing (+-2 px; it steps ~4 px down between x 600 and 700, beside a small lug at x 570). wing_tip_trailing is CONSTRUCTED: the common trailing-edge line meets the housing's tip-edge line (y = -0.00355 x + 3356.8) at (1732.4, 3350.6) (+-2 px); nothing physical is there, as the housing's aft edge is cut back. wing_upper_near_trailing_edge_1-6: the near-upper panel's trailing edge (+-1 px). Known planform points: wing_tip_trailing (111.1, 12.4 in the far-lower) is certain as a construction; the same trailing-edge line crosses the near-upper root line (y 1323) at (1531, 1323) and the body's silhouette midline at (1563, 1644.5). No leading edge, tip leading corner or root of the far-lower wing is visible (out of frame left, or behind the body and the loose wing), so the wing face cannot be tied to its planform by four non-collinear points from this photo alone: the chordwise scale must come from elsewhere. The near-upper panel's aft edge turns vertical below y ~1000 at x 1495-1498, 33 px forward of the straight trailing-edge line at the root: the existing wing_upper_near_root_trailing (1498, 1323) lies on that cut-back, not on the trailing-edge line, which meets the axis ~290-300 px (~1.6 in at the body's 185 px/in) ahead of the aft rim's centre (x ~1865), not 1.9 in. HOUSING (far-lower): housing_1-44 closed outline of the whole bare-metal piece, clockwise from its pointed forward apex (687.8, 3098.3): upper-left bevelled edge (half-level crossings, +-1.5 px), inboard edge (the top of a bright 15 px step strip, y 2986 to 2982.5, +-1 px), aft edge (+-1 px; parallel to and 21 px FORWARD of the wing's trailing-edge line), tip edge y 3351 (+-1 px), then straight across under the bracket's feet and the block (hidden from x 1530 to 1126), a V notch open at the tip (sides +-1.5 px, apex (1112, 3262) +-3 px), and the long lower-left edge back to the apex (half-level crossings of a dark band, +-2 px; points 816-994 straight within 3 px, slope 0.71). housing_face_1-10: the raised face's boundary, i.e. the inner edges of the upper-left bevel (a dark band 15-17 px wide) and of the inboard step strip (y ~2998-3001) (+-1.5 px). The step strip faces inboard and is lit; at this view its 15 px height means the housing face stands ~0.13 in proud of the wing face on this side. housing_hinge_1-4: a thin straight dark line across the housing parallel to the lower-left edge (valley minima, +-2 px; it fades out left of x 950); between it and the lower-left edge lies a ~1.1 in band shaded like a cylinder (dark, light, dark stripes, two dark holes at (850-865, 3180-3190) and (895-915, 3205-3225)), most likely the rolleron's hinge, which then runs diagonally from the forward apex out to the V notch at the tip edge. The V notch between the band's tip end and the flap's forward-tip corner is then the flap's clearance; the moving flap would be the part aft and inboard of housing_hinge. housing_slot_aft (1615, 3351): where the wheel's rim re-enters the housing's tip edge (+-2 px); the slot's forward end is hidden behind tip_block (the tooth circle predicts it at x ~1240). WHEEL: rolleron_rim_1-5 tooth tips and rolleron_root_1-5 tooth roots, left to right, on the wheel's silhouette below the tip edge, read from a red-minus-blue chroma image against the orange floor (+-1.5 px; rim_1 +-3 px, its face carries a highlight). The teeth are ratchet-shaped: a steep face on the forward side of each tip, a long face behind it. The 5 tips lie on one circle (residual 0.002 in) with an even pitch. bracket_1-36: the D-shaped bracket's outline on the housing face (radial and row edge crossings, +-1.5 px), its round end inboard, its legs to the tip edge, a foot running forward along the tip edge to x 1150, a cross-head screw in the foot (1270, 3335) and one at the aft leg's base (1475, 3330); closed along the tip edge (y 3351, assumed). bracket_inner_1-13: the arc of the D's recess (+-2 px; its straight sides are low-contrast, at x ~1345 and ~1479 +-4). bracket_arc_centre: the centre of a circle fitted to the D's outer arc (19 points, residual 0.01 in), +-2 px. The wheel's tooth circle is centred 16 px (~0.1 in) from it, so the D's round end is effectively concentric with the wheel: the bracket is most likely the axle's bearing bracket. The hub itself is under the bracket and NOT marked. tip_block_1-11: a rectangular block hanging below the tip edge under the bracket's forward foot (+-2 px), purpose unknown (a rolleron lock or the hinge's end fitting are candidates). trailing_edge_fitting_1-6: the aft outline of a dark lozenge-shaped fitting (y ~2897-3110) beside the housing's inboard-aft corner, standing ~36 px aft of the trailing-edge line (+-3 px where marked; its lower half, y 3050-3110, is too low in contrast to place and is not marked). housing_upper_near_1-9: the near-upper wing's housing, the bottom (inboard) edge of its bare-metal plate (+-1.5 px) and its aft end (x 1383-1389, 19 px forward of the trailing-edge line, matching the far-lower housing's 21 px). aft_block_1-24: the gold block on top of the motor at the aft end, outline above the body's top outline (y 1181) from where its raised front lip emerges from behind the near-upper wing (1497, 805) over the top (lip top 805-806, block top 823-825) and down the aft side to the body (1734.5, 1181) (+-1.5 px on the top and to y 960; +-4 px from y 990 to 1180 where a dark part on its aft side meets the dark background). nozzle_rim_1-18: the aft end's rim, its near half (where the grey tube meets the aft face, x ~1797-1833) and far half (outer silhouette, x ~1888-1932), +-1.5 px. ROUGH SIZES (far-lower tip region; local scales bracketed by mapping the trailing-edge line with the housings' inboard edges symmetric about the axis: 161-171 px/in chordwise, 115-127 px/in spanwise in the image; the same mapping places the housings' inboard edges 9.4-9.7 in from the axis): wheel tip-circle radius 1.42-1.46 in (diameter ~2.9 in), root circle ~1.30 in (tooth depth ~0.14 in), pitch 16.0-16.6 deg, i.e. 5 tips over 65 deg, ~22 teeth round; centre ~0.86 in inboard of the tip edge; protrudes 0.56-0.61 in beyond the TIP edge, and nothing protrudes aft of the trailing edge (the wheel's aft extent stays inside the housing's aft edge). Housing: 2.9-3.2 in spanwise from its inboard step to the tip; 5.1-5.4 in long along its inboard edge, 3.4-3.6 in along the tip edge from the notch to its aft corner, ~6 in from the forward apex to the aft edge; aft edge 0.13 in forward of the wing's trailing edge. D bracket: outer arc radius ~0.68 in, ~1.33 in across the legs, ~1.64 in from the arc's top to the tip edge. Gold block: ~1.9-2.0 in above the body's top outline (at the body's 185 px/in), flush with the aft rim, at least 1.9 in long (its front hidden). UNCERTAIN: the absolute local scale (+-5%), so the sizes above; the gold block's identity. NAVEDTRA 14313 fig 3-8 draws the aft hanger farther forward, beside the wings' forward roots, which here would be hidden behind the near-upper wing; this block sits aft of the trailing edge, ~2 in tall, its grey pedestal held by an axial socket-head cap screw. It may be a stand or handling fitting, so it is named aft_block, not hanger_aft. NOT MARKED: rolleron_hub (under the bracket, not visible); the slot's forward end (behind tip_block); the far-lower wing's root, leading edge and tip leading corner (hidden or out of frame); wing_root_shoe (the near-upper root sits on a rail at y 1323-1335 but its ends are not visible); nozzle_inner: the aft face shows a tan cork-like disc (probably a protective cover over the nozzle) inside grey and dark rings; only the far half of each ring is visible and none could be identified as the nozzle's throat or exit; the loose foreground wing's housing and wheel (out of focus, +-20 px); the near-lower and far-upper wings (not mounted).

dvids6457077_aim9m_canard_detail.view: from below, very close, looking up at the guidance section with the nose (yellow cover) to the left; focus is on the technician's face, the missile is out of focus
dvids6457077_aim9m_canard_detail.notes: VIEW: A technician fits a canard with a torque wrench from below. The guidance section runs along the top edge of the frame (stencil 'LOT NO.' visible), nose cover (yellow) at the left, x 150-1600; one canard hangs down at the right (x 2700-3598, being fastened, its root edge about y 230 with a visible gap to the body and a rounded aft root corner near (3345, 237)), a second canard's outer point shows at the centre near (2445, 690), and a third plate edge at the top right (x 3000-3150, y 0-200). MARKS: none. The camera is focused on the face; every missile edge is blurred over 10-20 px, and the edge profiles find no gradient strong enough to place a corner to 3 px. NOT MARKED: body pairs - the body's upper outline is above the frame everywhere, so no straight-across pair exists and the photo carries no scale; canard corners - out of focus, partly cut by the frame and crossed by the wrench and hands, and their near/far identity cannot be settled; dome, joints, lugs - out of frame or covered. DETAIL PASS (2026-11-09): VIEW: as in photos.json. MARKS: none. Every missile edge is blurred over 10-20 px (the canard hanging at right, x 2800-3600: its root edge at y ~230 from x 2900 to 3330 and its rounded aft root corner at (3330-3360, 230-260) are soft, and the body above it is out of frame), so nothing places to 3 px. NOT MARKED: canard_root_fitting (the root edge and its gap to the body show but are blurred ~15 px; no separate fitting is distinguishable); fuze windows, hangers (out of frame); body pairs (the body's outline is above the frame).

dvids9021997_aim9_nose_front34.view: front three-quarter from the left, nose nearest and to the left, camera about level; strong perspective (body about 1000 px across at the canards, about 310 px near the tail)
dvids9021997_aim9_nose_front34.notes: VIEW: Two Marines hold the round up to an F/A-18D; the camera is ahead of the left beam and close, so the nose is large at the left and the body recedes to the tail at x about 4700. Fins in X: four canards show, the near pair large and to the right (upper tip at the top right, lower tip at the bottom right), the far pair small and to the left. Edges on the missile are soft (focus is on the Marines), so every mark is +-3 px or as stated. MARKS: Body pair at x 1450 only (top against sky 1547 +-2; bottom 2541 +-3, low contrast against the dark aircraft behind); the axis runs nearly horizontal through the nose (y about 1970-1990) so the pair is vertical. Forward of the canards the outline is not cylindrical (the forward guidance section tapers toward the dome, as in the other photos), and between the canards and the tail the outlines are covered by the canards and hands or too soft. Canard roots: both near canards' root_leading marks are the rounded forward points of the canards inside the body silhouette. root_trailing is where the straight trailing edge (upper: from the tip with slope dy/dx -0.92; lower: dy/dx 1.23) meets the root plate along the body, +-4 px. The tip chords are not resolved in this view (each tip a point), so tip_leading = tip_trailing. NOT MARKED: nose, dome_top, dome_bottom - the nose is a rounded grey (matte, dirty) shape from x 83 (leftmost, y 1975) to about 1015, with a clear glass circle about 600 px across (centre about (712, 1965)) in its right half through which the seeker optics show; whether the grey shape is the dome glass, a cover or the tapered forward section could not be settled, so no dome joint or nose point is marked. Two dark brackets sit 180 deg apart just aft of the glass circle (top about x 560-860, y 1380-1600; bottom about x 500-810, y 2410-2650) - not hanger-shaped, not marked as lugs. Far canards (not marked): far-upper tip about (988, 1155), far-lower tip about (910, 2913). Wings at the tail, joints and the tail are small, soft and partly hidden by hands. DETAIL PASS (2026-11-09): VIEW: as in photos.json; focus is on the Marines, the missile's edges soft (2-6 px blur at the canards, worse aft). MARKS: none. Canard roots: each near canard's root is a straight edge along the body with a narrow gap (already marked in photos.json as root_leading/root_trailing); the near-upper canard shows a dark band ~30 px wide along its root from (1690, 1700) to (2220, 1880), its shaded face near the root seen obliquely, and the near-lower canard (sunlit) a plain root edge from (1660, 2400) to ~(2200, 2340). No separate root fitting (block, collar or fairing) stands out from either canard, so canard_root_fitting is not marked. Fuze windows: aft of the canards the near side carries a long raised fairing (x 2070-3200, y 1880-2400) with a chamfered forward end and screws, mostly under the Marines' hands, and the body aft of x ~3000 is out of focus (blur 15-25 px); no window band is visible, so fuze_window_* and fuze_band_* are not marked. The fairing's identity is unknown and its outline is covered by hands except its forward end, so it is not marked either. Two spring-loaded clamp brackets sit 180 deg apart just aft of the glass dome (top x 560-860, y 1370-1600, with a visible coil spring at x 700-850; bottom x 500-810, y 2410-2650); they are sharp but not hanger-shaped, their purpose is unknown, and the photo carries no station scale near them, so they are not marked. NOT MARKED: nose and dome (as in photos.json, the grey pointed shape left of the glass bubble is not settled as the missile's own nose); hangers (none visible); wings and tail (small, soft, partly hidden).

dvids9380788_aim120c_lau116_rear34.notes: VIEW: focus is on the armourer's face (x about 3000-3500); the whole aft end of the missile, the near control fin and the launcher are far out of focus (edges spread over 15-40 px), so almost nothing on the missile can be placed to 3 px. dvids9380790_aim120c_lau116_rear.fins: + as seen in the photo (one control fin hangs straight down in the image; the missile is X relative to its hooks, so the cheek-station launcher holds it canted about 45 deg)
dvids9380790_aim120c_lau116_rear.view: from behind and below, close and wide-angle; the camera is nearly on the missile's axis at the tail (the nozzle liner rim images as a circle 371 px wide by 379 px tall), a little right of it, so the body recedes to the upper left
dvids9380790_aim120c_lau116_rear.notes: VIEW: the nozzle face is almost square to the camera, so the body itself is seen nearly end-on and no outline pairs, joints, hooks or nose are measurable. MARKS: nozzle_* are where the orange liner meets the grey aft face, on a vertical and a horizontal line through its centre (red-minus-blue 50% level, checked visually; +-2 px). The lower fin hangs from the bottom of the control section just below the nozzle; the camera is behind and right, so its left boundary is the leading edge (farther) and the right the trailing edge (nearer). Its tip carries a red band (most likely a protective tip cover like the one with white lettering in dvids9380788; it may instead be red paint), so the two tip marks are the outer corners of that red band: where the fitted lower edge (y = 1775.2 + 0.119 (x - 1650)) meets the left edge (x about 1603) and the right silhouette (x about 2020); both corners are slightly rounded. If it is a cover, the true tip sits about 0.05 in inside it. fin_lower_root_trailing: the trailing-edge silhouette (2064 at y 1100, 2045 at 1300, 2018 at 1700, slanting) meets the body's lower outline at y about 984; a small root fairing at x 2075-2110, y 985-1030 confuses that corner (+-5 px). fin_lower_root_leading: the upper end of the fin's left boundary where it meets the body's lower edge (crisp), but that boundary is curved in this view (x 1700 at y 1050, 1645 at 1300, 1611 at 1500, then straight down at x 1597-1603 to the tip), so it is not certain the curved upper part is the leading edge itself rather than a root fairing. NOT MARKED: the other fins (one is hidden behind the body and launcher; a thin plate held edge-on in the armourer's left hand at x 2380-2770, y 740-812 could be the right-hand fin seen edge-on or a tool, so it is not marked); the LAU-116: no end of it can be identified. A long faired body with screws and a blunt rounded forward end runs along the missile's lower left from x about 1040 to 2000 (y 800-1080), with two small thin fins below it at x 1300-1380 and about 1000-1050; I could not identify it (a second store behind, or a fairing), and the lower fin's root lies along its bottom edge, so the root marks may be on that body rather than on the missile's cylinder. DETAIL PASS (2026-11-09): VIEW: from behind and a little right/below, nearly on the axis (liner rim 372 x 384 px), wide-angle and close; the body recedes to the upper left, so the aft face's outline on the left is not a silhouette.
